text:
B: Alright! How you doing? Liam.
A: Hiya Liam, I'm Joanne. Ooh, I like your records behind you.
B: Cheers. Don't look too close, half of them want a dust. Where are you, then?
A: Warrington. Great Sankey.
B: No way! I'm Latchford. Small world, that. Two Warringtonians, what are the odds.
A: Oh, I'm made up, someone who talks properly. Is that a car logo on your top?
B: Yeah, I'm in sales at a dealership on the edge of town. New, used, finance, the lot. Senior sales exec, if we're being fancy.
A: I knew it! I said, he looks like the lads in sales. I'm in sales too, sort of. I'm a team leader at a contact centre up at Birchwood, broadband and TV. Retentions mainly, so people ring up to cancel and we talk them out of it.
B: Oh, so you're the ones! I rang up to cancel mine last year and some girl had me on a better deal in about four minutes. Dead good at it, she were.
A: Probably one of mine, to be fair. My figures were the best on the floor for years, that's how I got made team leader. It's all reading people, do you know what I mean? You know within ten seconds if they mean it or they just want money off.
B: That's it, that's it exactly. Same on the forecourt. They walk in, you clock what they've parked in, how they're stood, you know if they're buying today. I sold three on Saturday. Top of the board for the month.
A: Get you! Listen, my Gary's van's just failed its MOT, so I might be giving you a ring.
B: Ha, go on then. What's he drive?
A: A Transit, it's ancient. He's a plasterer, so it's full of dust and bags of skim.
B: We don't do a lot of vans, to be honest, but I'd find him something. I'll sort you out. Mate's rates.
A: I'll hold you to that. Are you a Wolves man?
B: Course. Through me dad. I only get to a few games a season, like. Me mum's from Huyton, so I get Liverpool rammed down me throat the rest of the time.
A: Oh, we've got season tickets, me and Gary. Were you there Friday? We were robbed. That ref wants his eyes testing.
B: I watched it in the pub. Shocking. Absolutely shocking. Jess had me at a garden centre all Saturday after, so it were a bad weekend all round.
A: Is that your girlfriend?
B: Yeah, six years. She's a dental nurse. The cat's hers, technically. Nacho. He sleeps on me decks.
A: Aw. We've got a cockapoo, Bella. She's had to go to the groomer's again, cost me a fortune. Do you DJ then?
B: Now and then, at a bar in town when me mate needs someone. Disco, house, bit of northern soul. Nothing major.
A: My son's twenty-three, he'd love that. He's an apprentice sparky, he's always out in Manchester.
B: Tell him to come down. Did you get through that puzzle at the start, by the way? I just guessed.
A: Erm, I think I did alright, actually. I got most of it.
B: Course you did. I could tell you were a high achiever, me.
A: Charmer! See, you're doing it now, aren't you, reading me.
B: Can't switch it off, Joanne. Occupational hazard. What's the traffic like your end? The Bridge Foot roundabout this morning, I'm telling you, I nearly...
